- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias to counteract underestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in periods of high volatility or sentiment uncertainty; add 0.3–0.8 point upward adjustment if sentiment is flat or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model often drifts toward historical mean; apply slight downward bias to avoid overconfidence in recent highs.
